title: MCAS Iwakuni children participate in Pillowcase Project (Package/Pkg)
description: After the devastation of Hurricane Katrina in 2006, the American Red Cross found pillowcases were better suited for packing the essentials rather than plastic bags.  Lance Cpl. Jaxson Fryar went to Iwakuni Elementary school to check out a special project the Red Cross had to offer. This video story includes soundbites from Tammie Pech, Omaha Nebraska, and Keith Carr, Florence, Mississippi. This story is available in high definition.

transcript.text: - Question one. How quickly should you -
- [Narrator] Iwakuni Elementary School students
participated in a Pillowcase Project
focused on increasing awareness during natural hazards.
American Red Cross instructors led the course
discussing safety, emotional management ideas,
and demonstrated steps to take during an earthquake.
American Red Cross Regional Program Manager Tammy Pech
expects the training will help children stay safe.
- We hope that this Pillowcase Project
brings children the realization that they can be prepared.
One part of the program that we do
has a coping skill with it,
helping them become more prepared
and hoping that they're able to handle
the stress of an emergency.
It's also a day to day activity.
- [Narrator] The participating fifth grade student
each received a pillowcase to illustrate
what contents the fabric will hold,
then packed them with the essential supplies.
Iwakuni Elementary School's Liaison Officer says
this training offers lifelong benefits
in emergency preparedness.
- I would love for the student to
keep in mind what they learned,
and in the event of any incident
they cannot only help themselves,
but help their fellow students as well.
This being the fifth graders,
they have a little bit of edge on the other students
because they are somewhat stuck as leaders,
and they can have some inspiration.
- [Narrator] This is the first month
the Pillowcase Project has happened on
Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni.
Reporting from Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni Japan
I'm Lance Corporal Jackson Friar.
(children talking)
